title: The Missing Calibration Observer
concept: Autonomous observatory calibration constructs a humanlike target over an empty crew chair.
ownership: Every named apparatus, object, shape and action in this testcase is agent-owned staging; none is a requester-required fact, anchor or lock. Testcase is frozen independently before retrieval to test output realization.

random_selection.author: space_arm_c
random_selection.method: 16 random bytes modulo four independently authored broad scene families
random_selection.ownership: All scene-family choices are agent-owned; none are requester requirements.

reference.scope: visible facial and hair appearance only; no actual identity, age, personality or history inference

expected_visible_relations.expected: Pressure window and planetary limb or recognizably outer-space exterior visible with the engineer and internal equipment.
Pale chair cushion, open straps and space above cushion are visibly empty beneath the suspended target.
Matte-black oval and two shoulder-width paddles suggest a seated human outline while visible rods identify their mechanical support.
Two articulated sensor heads point their optical apertures toward the suspended apparent head rather than the actual engineer; gantry support is visible.
Engineer looks at the apparatus while a rail-supported hand stops short of the recessed red interrupt control; face, hand and target relationship is readable.
Visible short dark bob, fine fringe and broad facial appearance are consistent with the portrait at usable face scale. This is appearance similarity, not identity proof.

review_rule: Review actual saved pixels; author observability as visible, partial or unobservable. A multi-component relation only passes when all components and their relation are visible together. Prompt/audit metadata is not pixel evidence.
